utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are proceeding with Witness A. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined continued by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness A. Yesterday I only got a chance to introduce myself and put just a couple of questions to you. If you remember, I asked you how many times have you talked to the Prosecutor, and you told me that the first interview was in 1994, and at that time you also signed the statement given by you to the Prosecutor. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I think the witness is saying that he can't hear well, or he has trouble with interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the usher please assist the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear the interpreters. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you hear me, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In that case, I will repeat. Your first interview with the Prosecution took place in 1994, at which time you also signed your written statement. This is what I said, that we have a written statement given by you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then you went on to confirm to me that you had talked to the Prosecutor, or rather, with the representatives of the OTP, in 2001 as well, in Odzak, and that you also had interviews with them in June of this year. At that time, you did not sign any statements; you simply had interviews with them. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your last interview with the Prosecution, as far as I could tell from your 92 bis Rule statement, you were -- also presented several things that you had said during your earlier statements; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your last interview with the Prosecution, you were confronted with allegations you made when giving a statement in 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now you stated a number of new things and a number of supplemental claims to that initial statement, is that right, to this last statement that you gave recently? What I'm trying to say is that you supplemented this last statement in a number of ways. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second, or rather, the third interview that I had in Odzak with the representatives of the OTP is not a really detailed interview, similar to the one that we had in 1994. The investigators simply asked me whether things were such-and-such, and then I would reply yes or no, and this is how the conversation went along. Therefore, they did not insist very much on my stay in prison, in the cell, and they also did not insist a lot on the torture that I underwent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me also add that when giving my first statement, some things were not recorded verbatim as I described them, or perhaps some things were not translated accordingly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Today, during our cross-examination, we will go back to that statement of yours and you will have an opportunity to clarify certain matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the Exhibit 532, which is the witness's statement, to be put in front of the witness so that we can go over certain paragraphs in that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your last statement, I saw that you described in detail the exchanges that took place in Samac municipality before the war broke out. You described that in paragraphs 14, 15, 16, and 17 of your statement. I don't think we need to analyse that now. There's no need for you to look at those paragraphs just now. But my question is as follows: We are now referring to the exchanges between, let's say, Yugoslavia and Croatia, which took place in 1991 in Samac municipality. Do you remember that Izet Izetbegovic also participated in organising these exchanges, and at that time he was the head of the civilian protection staff in Bosanski Samac? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And as far as I know, he never held that post, the post of the head of the civilian protection staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how many exchanges there were? I'm again referring to these pre-war exchanges.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you: I think that there were two or perhaps three of them. I'm sure about two exchanges. I'm not quite sure about the third one. However, I know that during 1991, a lot of buses came from the territory of Yugoslavia that we had to escort to Croatia, and these buses were not recorded anywhere. There was -- the president of the Red Cross would be there, a bus would arrive, mostly filled with women, children, and the elderly, and then in that same bus they would be transported to Slavonski Samac, which is in Croatia, immediately after the bridge or the Sava River. And then another bus would wait for them there and take them to another location unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I know, in 1991, there was freedom of movement for all vehicles on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, this is how it was until the 17th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you saw that these people -- that the buses on the other side in Croatia were awaiting these people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Vinko Dragicevic, who had at the time was the head of the SUP, appointed you to be a member or the head of the delegation in charge of these exchanges; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He appointed me, Namik Suljic, Gregurovic Luka, Mujkanovic Sead, Loncaric Dragan was there as well. There were other members of the police involved in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to progress as quickly as possible. I'm mostly interested in the information that pertains to you. Do you remember that the lists for exchanges were coordinated in the public security station in Samac? Do you have any information to this effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that I was in the MUP building, or in front of it, where at the time members of the JNA were as well, as were members of the special military police; again, the representatives of the JNA. I remember well Major General Tumanov. There were two other lieutenant colonels and colonels there, and two or three other persons in the JNA uniforms, whereas on the Croatian side there were two men. Our task was to take over people on the bridge and take them to the station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has already confirmed the identity of certain persons that I would like to focus on now, and I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit D52/ter [as interpreted]. [In English] D52/3 ter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an excerpt from a newspaper article describing these exchanges, and I would like you to read just the first paragraph of that article, and then I will ask you whether you know more about things described in that article. Please let me know when you have read this. So the first paragraph only, please. What I would like you is to confirm whether you know -- or did you know a person who at the time represented the Croatian side, Stjepan Adanic? Do you remember that person coming to take part in negotiations that took place in the Samac police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that the then Minister of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Alija Delimustafic, also came, as did his deputy, Vitomir Zepinic? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Not this question, but the previous question, again, a slight problem with two questions, and the answer doesn't indicate what the witness is agreeing to. He's asked: "Do you know this man Stjepan Adanic? " And secondly: "Do you remember he took part in negotiations that took place in the Samac police station?" Answer, "Yes." So what is the answer "yes"? Yes, he knows Adanic or yes he remembers him coming to take part in negotiations in the Samac police station or yes, both, I know him and he also came to Bosanski Samac? It should be clear, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It seems that I'm trying to be too efficient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you know this man? Please tell me that first. Did you hear of him? Did you know him, Stjepan Adanic, at the time, who was one of the senior officers in the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know Mr. Stjepan Adanic, nor did I ever personally meet him. Out of all of those people who were present at the exchange, representing both sides, and representatives of the Ministry of the Interior, the only person I knew and knew the office held by that person was Mr. Delimustafic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that Mr. Delimustafic was present at the Samac police station when negotiations between these two parties took place? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that he was at the police station, upstairs, on the floor. I didn't go upstairs, and I think that he was probably upstairs with this other officer, Tumanov, and a few more officers. His driver was downstairs, sitting in the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's quite enough. Thank you. Do you know that the newspaper Oslobodjenje was printed at that time and during the war in Sarajevo and was published there? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oslobodjenje exists even to this day. It probably existed even then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are not sure as to whether it was published then? You're not sure about that? Or let me ask you another thing: Do you know whether Oslobodjenje is published in Sarajevo today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Oslobodjenje exists as a publication. I know that it can be purchased in the Federation, in the BH Federation. As to who is the publisher, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. During your chief examination on the 8th of July, you first described how you were interrogated at the SUP building by Milos Savic, the inspector. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Q. On page 10, 743, you said that he had ordered a coffee for you and told you that should somebody in a camouflage uniform walk in, that he was going to say that the coffee was his. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on what we know here, it was members of the special units from Serbia who wore camouflage uniforms, and yesterday you said it was mostly members of the special units that beat you, members of these special units from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: These specials, these people that were not from our area and whom I didn't know before, who spoke in a different dialect, they wore these multicoloured camouflage uniforms. There were several persons from our municipality who also wore that kind of uniform. I will also add that Nebojsa Stankovic, called Cera, had the same kind of uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that it was these people, including those whom you've just mentioned, who beat you the most? This is how I understood your yesterday's response, that the members of the special units beat you the most.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, including Stevan Todorovic, who was not from Serbia, and some people who escorted him and who were from Samac municipality. However, I don't remember their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go on. Tell me, please: While you worked in the Samac police, when a person who was arrested underwent interrogation, was it typical for the interrogator to offer coffee for the detainee? Was it typical?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was doing my job, I did not have the need to conduct any interviews, and I can also say that if it were an official interview, so to speak, an investigative interview, then I can say that there certainly was no coffee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll agree that this interview that Milos Savic conducted with you, that this was an official investigative interview; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it probably was, because he held the appropriate post. I mean, he was in a position to question me, and I was not in a position to question him. But I don't know whether he was indeed the authorised person to question me and whether all the other persons that conducted such interviews were properly authorised to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that was not my question. But did you understand this offer of a coffee as a gesture of goodwill on the part of your colleague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to Mr. Milos Savic, who had worked with me - we knew each other well - I already said two days ago in my testimony -- I stated that he felt uncomfortable because of the fact that he had to talk to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice that this man was frightened of those specials from Serbia? Did he say anything to that effect to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already said, he offered me coffee. The coffee was brought in and he told me that if the people in camouflage uniforms were to enter, he was going to say that the coffee was his.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to speculate any more as to his relationship to these men. I want to know whether he mistreated you or threatened you or physically abused you in the course of that interview.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you had the opportunity to read your statement and to sign it, I mean the statement that you gave the second time when he dictated the statement to the typist and then you had the opportunity to read it and to sign it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was read back to me. I don't remember what kind of a statement I gave. I believe that I did sign it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more technical issue: Did he dictate the statement to the typist in front of you? Were you present while he was dictating the statement to the typist, the statement that you later on had the opportunity to read and to sign?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll move on to another topic. You described how you saw Miroslav Tadic in the SUP when he talked to Mato Perkovic. You testified about that on page 10762 of the transcript in front of this Trial Chamber. Let me first read to you a sentence from your statement given in the year 1994 to the OTP. That's page 23 of the English version of the statement, for the benefit of my colleagues from the Prosecution. You stated the following: "Miroslav Tadic came to the prison once. Miroslav Tadic, Brcko. He called out Mato Perkovic, told him to come out into the corridor. He said that he had spoken to his brother over the radio and that he would be exchanged." Do you remember having stated that to the Prosecutors? Could you please just say yes or no and then we will analyse further. Can you just tell me whether you remember stating that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that Mr. Miroslav Tadic came twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you whether this is what you stated in 1994. Just tell me whether this is what you stated to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I probably did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like photograph 52 from the Exhibit P14 to be placed in front of the witness. It's the same photograph that Mr. Lazarevic analysed together with the witness, because I believe it would be helpful. [In English] 52. No, no. It's P14, photograph 52.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, this is the photograph that we had already looked at yesterday; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the area where you were, in one of these cells, together with Mr. Franjo Barukcic and Mr. Mato Perkovic and Mr. Dragan Lukac were in the cell next door; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please indicate now, although you did mention that yesterday, in which cell you were, I mean you and Mr. Barukcic, and in which cell the other two men were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mato Perkovic and Mr. Dragan Lukac were in the first cell, and in this cell here, right next to the window, there were myself and Mr. Franjo Barukcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let the record reflect that the witness indicated the first cell as the cell which is closer to the entrance, and the cell number 2 is the cell which is further down the corridor, down at the bottom of the corridor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see another fact here; I noticed it yesterday. It seems to me that the doors to the cells themselves are bars, so it is possible to see what is going on inside. Are these bars the kind of bars that allow the air to circulate? That's the way I see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain this to you. These were the bars, and there was no insulation whatsoever. So we in the cell were able to hear people speaking even at a distance of 10 to 15 metres. If a car's engine would go on on the other side of the road, you could hear that too. And I can also tell you that I had such a powerful instinct that we knew exactly when somebody would arrive in a car, because the engine would go off, and we knew that that person would enter our cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to concentrate on my questions, because I would like to go through them as quickly as possible. My client claims that he did not enter any of the two cells but that a guard took Mato Perkovic out into the corridor, where the greetings from his brother were transferred to him. Is it quite possible, in light of your statement in 1994, in which you also said that Mr. Mato Perkovic was brought out into the corridor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that Mr. Miroslav Tadic came to the door. I saw him personally. Now, whether he was accompanied by a guard or not, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he didn't enter your cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you testified about this event here before the Trial Chamber, you indicated that you didn't hear the conversation between Mato Perkovic and Miroslav Tadic, that in fact Mato Perkovic told you later on about the conversation. Do you remember testifying to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, ten years have passed, and such a long time has its impact. When I saw Mr. Miroslav Tadic, I immediately thought that there would be an exchange. I stated before this Trial Chamber, and also to the investigators, I cannot remember right now whether I heard the words spoken by Mr. Tadic or whether I heard it from Mato, but I do know that they did discuss the exchange, or in other words, first he said that he had spoken to his brother, and he relayed the greetings, and Mato wanted to know whether his parents were still alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already testified to that, Witness A. That's not in dispute. What is in dispute, however, is that a few days ago you stated to this Trial Chamber that you weren't able to hear the conversation and that Mato Perkovic told you about it. Things are very important for us. Some things are really important, and it's much better for you to say that you don't remember than to say something that would not be correct or accurate? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, Ms. Reidy has obtained the examination-in-chief, and the answer that I can see here is -- I asked him: "Can you recall what they spoke about?" And the witness, Witness A, said: "I could overhear, and later on Mato told me about this. He told me that Miroslav had a telephone conversation with his brother," and so on and so forth. So he said, A, "I could overhear it"; and B, "I was told about it as well." So it's not -- 10763 -- sorry, 2, at the very bottom of 10762: "Can you recall what they spoke about?" "I could overhear, and later on Mato told me about it." So he said both: He could hear it and he was told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask my colleague from the Prosecutor to read the next two lines, on the next page, on page 10763. [In English] "[Previous translation continues] ... we simply asked Mato, Mato what's going to happen?" MR. DI FAZIO: Of course, but that's not inconsistent. Of course they would ask him what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't want to dwell on this topic too long. I just want to ask from the witness if he's able to provide us with this information or not. Today we heard from the witness that he was able to hear what was going on, the conversation, at a distance of 10 to 15 metres. I just want to ask the witness whether he heard the conversation between Mato Perkovic and Miroslav Tadic. Let him answer the question now. I think that's the easiest solution. MR. DI FAZIO: That's fine. That's fine. I've got no problem with that. But I don't want it being put to the witness that he said in examination-in-chief that he didn't hear it. He said: "I could overhear it," and it was also reported to him. It's as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That has been clarified sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I then ask the witness whether he heard the conversation himself, or do you think that this has been cleared up? Could we ask him to state clearly whether he heard the conversation or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can ask him. The witness should be able to answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness A, we have a very, very simple question here. I don't want to trap you in any way. Do you remember now whether you heard the conversation between Mr. Tadic and Mr. Perkovic from inside your cell? That's my question to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I already stated that one could hear it, but I couldn't hear every word. I heard the word "mother," "alive." So I really didn't feel the need to listen in to their conversation, because I knew that Mato would tell us why he had come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think that's quite enough. You also stated in your statement that both you and Mr. Perkovic looked really bad. You said yourself that you looked worse. You said that Tadic came several days after you had been transferred to the SUP building from the garage of the SUP. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been in the second half of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's what I think too. Let me remind you. On page 10764, you said that it was sometime in mid-June, since you were exchanged 10, 15, or 20 days later, and it is not contentious that you were exchanged on the 5th and that in fact you left to be exchanged on the 4th. My question to you is: Do you know that before that, in Samac, there had been only one exchange while you were still in Serbia? Do you know about that fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were held in the SUP garage, you described before the Trial Chamber and in your statement how Stevan Todorovic came with his police officers, and if I understand it correctly, this is when you underwent the most severe maltreatment and beatings, compared to the entire period of your incarceration. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he came to the SUP garage, while you were detained there, he had not yet -- he was not involved in a car accident that you heard about later on when you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you to a part of your statement. I'm again referring to the statement from year 1994. That's page 23 in B/C/S, and for my learned colleagues from the Prosecution, that's on page 24. You described how you went to be exchanged, how you were put on the bus, and you stated the following: "While I sat on the bus, I heard that Stevan Todorovic was involved in a traffic accident and that he was in a hospital in Brcko. I realised that I probably wouldn't have been released had it not been for the accident." Do you remember having stated that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember quite clearly, and I remember who told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's precisely what I'm interested in. Could you please tell us: Who gave you that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got that information -- or rather, the person that told us this on the bus, on the 4th, in fact, as we were travelling by bus -- that was Djuheric, nicknamed Coc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the thing that you just told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now remind ourselves. Djuheric, nicknamed Coc, was a member of the armed forces, not of the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mr. Coc. I knew him even at the time when he was a member of the 4th Detachment. Now, as to -- in what capacity he was there on the bus I don't know, but I do know that he was not in the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of the proceedings, I came to understand that you were one of the persons who was beaten the most severely, most severely in Samac, and the person who sustained the gravest injuries. Do you think that Todorovic would have prevented you to go to be exchanged even in light of this condition that you were in? MR. DI FAZIO: It's fathoming -- the mind of Stevan Todorovic would be difficult for anyone, let alone this witness, so I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You're asking the witness to speculate, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Coc tell you that Stevan Todorovic personally wouldn't allow you to be exchanged, even though you were in the condition that you described to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he spoke in general. He wasn't referring only to me. He said that he had broken his leg somewhere in the vicinity of Brcko and that he was in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, he said if he were here, you would not be exchanged. I think he was referring to the bus that he was escorting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand from the question asked by my colleague Mr. Lazarevic, and from your previous statements, the persons that approached the bus while you were in Lipovac wanted to take you personally off the bus. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's remember another episode. Do you remember that at the checkpoint near Krepsic, a police officer also wanted to take you off the bus to prevent you from being exchanged? Do you remember that also?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know that police officers from Samac manned that checkpoint? Do you remember that, or do you know that fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember who was manning that checkpoint. Let me just tell you: I was preoccupied with the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you don't remember, we'll not dwell on that any more. I don't know if the photograph had already been removed. I wanted to ask another question. Great. I'm interested in another thing, and I believe that we will be able to elicit this on the basis of this photograph. On page 10765, you described how Jovanovic approached you and told you you would be exchanged. On page 10764 you said that you were overjoyed. You also said that he came to the window to tell you that because he didn't want you to look suspicious. Do you remember having stated that? Can you please confirm whether this is the window that he approached?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see this window here. This window had two window panes, one, two. There were bars here. I was here. So I was able to look out into the yard, and we could hear what was going on, the conversations, when shifts would change. But let me not go into that. And on the 4th of July, I heard, through this window, somebody speaking in a very low voice. Slobodan was calling my name, very softly. I peered out, and he told me, "You will be exchanged today." And he immediately asked -- Lukac immediately asked me what was going on, and I told him that he had told me that we would be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you've already explained all this to us. I would just like the record to reflect that the witness again indicated the position where he was - that was the cell closest to the window - and also the place on the window from where Jovanovic called him and told him this sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he spoke very softly to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we remove the photograph?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We don't need it any more. You probably don't want this photograph to be in front of your eyes. So you said that he said this very softly to you, and the transcript reflects that he came to tell you that so that you wouldn't look suspicious. I don't quite understand this. Suspicious to whom? How would you look suspicious?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I will read you what you said on page 10765. This is the transcript of July 16th, or rather, this is the transcript of the 8th. So your testimony on the 8th of July was as follows, page 10765, line 9. [In English] "He called out my name from the courtyard, and he approached to the wall so that he could -- that he would not be conspicuous." [Interpretation] That's what I wanted to know: What does it mean, that he didn't want to be conspicuous?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how was this translated into English. What I was trying to say was that he called me in such a voice so as to prevent others allegedly around him from hearing him. He didn't want others to know that he called me and talked to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By saying "others," do you mean policemen and others who were there in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had a feeling that he came to tell me that in such a way that others could not hear him calling me and saying this to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's how I understood it as well. But I also know that all of the exchanges were public, that lists were read out publicly, that people were informed about exchanges publicly. You just told us that you had a feeling that he wanted to say this to you secretly so that others wouldn't hear this. Can you tell me: Why did you have that feeling? Why didn't he come to tell you that publicly in front of others? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I object. It's strictly impossible for this witness to explain to you why Jovanovic was concerned about attracting attention to himself. But perhaps even more importantly is it's not particularly helpful to any issue, is it, with respect?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think -- MR. DI FAZIO: This guy approaches the witness and doesn't want people to know that he's reporting that he's going to be exchanged. It's -- how can it help us one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What the witness has answered and what he has described how he was told is sufficient, Mr. Lukic. We've dwelt on this for too long.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree, Your Honours. I'm not going to put any questions regarding this, but I will reply to the Prosecutor and reiterate that I believe that the manner in which this man approached him is extremely important. Now we'll switch to the other matters regarding your exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that there was a delay at the bridge in Raca, that you had to way for a long time at the bridge in Raca in order to cross in the FRY, Federal Republic of Yugoslavia? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I remember is that there was a delay while we were en route, somewhere near Bijeljina. One of the buses had a breakdown, and since it already became dark --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already described this. We don't need to go back to that. You also described yesterday the course of the execution and the line to which you were brought near Lipovac, where you were exchanged. Do you remember those other people who were escorting you, Coc and the others, coming to that line where you were exchanged? Were they able to get to that point with the weapons that they had on them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also described the kinds of people that went with you from Samac. You said that there were women, children, and the elderly there. On page 10766, you said that in the playground of the elementary school they saw people mostly from Hasici, Croatian Tisina, mostly Croats and that there were some Muslims there as well. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like now to move on to the exchange itself and exchange lists, but prior to that I want to inform the Trial Chamber that there are six exchange lists pertaining to this exchange. All of these were exhibits of the Prosecution, obviously available to them. And in view of the kinds of questions I'm going to put, I would like all six lists to be given to the witness. Four of these lists have already been introduced, one of them as an ID document. In order for you to be able to follow this, I would like to say that there are three lists of the people who were exchanged from the Serbian side and three lists from the HVO, from the Croatian side. And I would like to cover this very quickly with the witness, to see whether he's able to identify any of these people on these lists. Therefore, I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit D12/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What are you trying to establish?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, all I'm trying to do is to show to the Trial Chamber that the same number of people was exchanged from both sides and that the composition of the group exchanged was approximately the same. There were some other witnesses that gave evidence regarding this exchange. All I'm interested in is the number of people exchanged on both sides, and I would also like to see whether the witness knows any of them. Let me also tell you what I consider to be important, Your Honours. Yesterday the Prosecution put a question regarding Mr. Zaric and negotiations involving some pilots. The witness, on the other hand, said, in his 92 bis statement, that the specials from Serbia, or some man called Laki, asked, "How much do you want us to ask for you?" So in view of that, I just want to confront this witness and ask whether he's aware of the fact whether the exchange was one-for-one, that the same number of people was exchanged on both sides. And that's what I'm trying to say. I hope it will not take long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I'm trying to look at, whether there's any dispute from the Prosecution as to whether the numbers were different. MR. DI FAZIO: Well I haven't conducted that analysis, if Your Honours please, and I'm sure that Mr. Lukic is probably right, but until I've had an opportunity for myself to go through, I'm not prepared --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you're not able to say. MR. DI FAZIO: So I can't say that. But couldn't we just -- couldn't we just adduce it from the documents? Is it not possible for anyone to just look at the documents rather than asking this witness? I don't know. We might be able to save time in that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The documents -- the lists you want to show the witness, some of them are new, they haven't been discussed before?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. You can introduce them, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could introduce just these two remaining lists that have not been introduced yet, to give them an ID number, because we don't have the English translation for them yet. These are Prosecutor's documents, and then later on we will be able just to add up the numbers and to show you what we are trying to prove. Perhaps the witness is already acquainted with these lists. One of them is a list of men that departed, and the other one is the list of men that arrived. And we can also introduce this during our case as well. We have a way to prove how these lists were compiled. But I think it would be convenient to introduce them as ID documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, you can take this back. So the document I want to show the witness now is the list of persons exchanged, the persons that departed on the 4th of July, 1992. And a similar list is under the number D12. There is a total of 100 persons on this list. This document has already been delivered to the Prosecution. I will ask the witness to take a brief look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's not the list that you are looking at now, Witness A. The usher will give you the relevant list. And I will tell you just briefly: Since you told us that you saw that on that playground there were Croats from Hasici and Tisina, are you able to recognise the names of any of the individuals on this list? Were any of them exchanged together with you? MR. DI FAZIO: It's D12 is being shown now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which list --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- is the witness looking at?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is looking at the entirely new list which was just given to him, and there are 100 names on that list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that right, Witness A?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because D12 has 52 persons on the list. If you recognise any of the names, please tell us; if not, then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a bit difficult for me to read this. The print is very small and there are many people there. The names that I'm looking at right now, the names of the people that were not with me on the bus. Okay. Under number 71, I remember that person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just read out the name, and it will be enough for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Karalic Ivo Zlatko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you remember that he was exchanged with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and so was Senic Juro, Tufekovic Marko, and that here on the first page, let me just see. Djuro Petricevic, son of Marko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that will be enough for me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just add that the people who were on list number 2 were with me on the bus, the list containing 52 persons. These are the people that were with me on the bus. And I had no contact with other people. But I just remember seeing these faces on the tape and after we were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's quite enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we just give an ID number to this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be D72/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And another document, which in view of the Defence completes the picture of this exchange. This is the document supplied by the Croatian side, dated 4th July, 1992, containing 52 male names. This is also a document of the Prosecution. I don't believe the witness will know individuals from this list, because they're mostly Serbs from Odzak municipality, but I will ask a question pertaining to a signature and a stamp on this document. Sir, you can see three rather unclear signatures here. But in view of the fact that you stated that after your treatment you volunteered to work in Orasje as an intelligence officer, perhaps you knew or you heard of Ivica Matanovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just heard of him; I never saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know Mr. Mija Matanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know Mija before the war. We met afterwards, and I know him well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what was his job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was involved in exchanges. I don't know within what organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm interested in another person. Yesterday you described the telephone conversation that your wife overheard, and in connection with that, you said that you knew Anto Kujic. Do you also know that he was the security officer of the Croatian army, of Croatia, during those events in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know him at all, nor do I know what was his function in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps we can have this latest one marked for identification, the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, and yes, I agree with you. We need an ID number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will actually be marked D71/3 ter ID. A number was skipped, so we're going back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be D71/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on, when you were exchanged, and in view of the fact what you said Tadic had told you during the exchange, did you later on acquire any information regarding the Serbs imprisoned in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now turn to another event described by you on the 8th of July. You described the conversation you had with Mr. Franjo Barukcic. That's on page 35 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just one clarification: You told us you didn't know Anto Kujic; however, you said that your wife had told you that he was there during the negotiations. What I'm interested in is whether your wife ever told you what was his function, what tasks he was involved in. Did your wife know Kujic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't ask her. That same Kujic was present when I was exchanged, and that was the first time I saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't know where he was employed. I didn't hear an answer. You didn't know where he was employed and on whose behalf he was there at the exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know where he was employed. I suppose that he worked on the other side. Now, whether he worked for the HV or the HVO, I don't know. I wasn't interested in that. I was exchanged, and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You described in detail your conversation with Mr. Franjo Barukcic on the 8th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a very brief line of questioning, some ten minutes remaining, so should we make a break now and leave that for -- or leave that for tomorrow? All I'm interested in is this conversation with Mr. Barukcic, and that will be the last topic I will cover.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have to break because of the other arrangements with the other witness. So we'll continue tomorrow, most likely after the Status Conference, so whatever time the Status Conference will be through, parties should be around the building. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. If Your Honours please, I don't know what happened yesterday with the other witness in the United States and the videolink; I wasn't here. But I'm concerned to make sure, if possible, that we make sure that Witness A is finished tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure that will happen. I'm sure we'll be able to finish him, because the videolink witness is moving fairly fast. MR. DI FAZIO: All right. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Except that the witness -- this witness will have to come much later tomorrow, after the Status Conference. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Yes. Very well. Thank you. It would, of course, be ideal for him to finish tomorrow, because we're not sitting on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If he doesn't finish tomorrow, then he's got Friday, Saturday, Sunday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because Mr. Lukic said he has only ten more minutes he requires and that's the last counsel, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. Ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And thereafter it will be -- MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic. Yes. How much do you think you'll needed?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm also very mindful about this fact, and I will try to reduce the cross-examination as much as possible. Well, if the witness will be cooperative, according to the standards in cross-examination, with yes or no answers, maybe half an hour, 40 minutes, something like that, but -- plus re-direct. And then I don't know how we shall conduct videolink examination, because -- MR. DI FAZIO: I've got no re-direct so far of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. All right. MR. DI FAZIO: Possibly one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO: That's it so far. I can't guarantee that that will be the case tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We'll continue our proceedings at 1600 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic. You are cross-examining.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Subasic. I will continue my examination. You said that the pistol that you had in Mebos during those war days in Bosanski Samac was something that you took home with you. So I'd like to ask you whether, on your way to work or on your way back home, did you have anything on you that would prevent you from being arrested, in view of the fact that you had a weapon on you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had my security guard uniform on me, and this is how I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have some kind of insignia on that uniform?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it said on it "Mebos company."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Krgovic. I wonder, Mr. Subasic: I seem to recall -- I could be wrong, but I seem to recall that yesterday you said you didn't wear a uniform when you acted as a security guard. Could you clarify that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. I didn't have a uniform before the war, and it was not mandatory either, but when the war broke out, since I was the only employee there for several days, I was issued with a uniform from my employer, and I only wore it for those several days during the war. That uniform was seized when I was arrested. It was seized on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, you didn't have a white band or anything like that, did you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You are a Muslim, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And during those days you moved freely about Samac without the white band?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's some 80 metres between my company and my apartment, and I didn't move anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, you were transferred to the elementary school from Bijeljina sometime around 13th of May, 1992; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When were you transferred from Bijeljina to the elementary school building?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all. I was transferred to the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So it was the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then the following day you were transferred elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when was that? It was on the 13th or 14th of May, 1992, was it?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. It was mid-May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify something for the transcript. So on the following day you were transferred to the elementary school building; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then sometime in mid-August you were transferred from the school building to the TO building?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean from the elementary school building to the TO building?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, on page 78, in replying to a question, you said that you saw Mr. Tadic while you were in the elementary school building but you did not know how many times he came there, although every time there was an exchange, he would come there. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You never saw Tadic in the TO building; is that right? That's what you said in your statement to the Prosecution in 1998. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I never saw him in the TO building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So that means that these visits of Mr. Tadic to the elementary school must have happened in the time period between mid-May 1992 until mid-August of that same year; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, there were other fellow citizens with you in the elementary school. You will read out some names to you and you can tell me whether you remember these people. Do you remember Hasan Bicic? Was he there with you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And his brother, Muhamed Bicic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was Dragan Delic with you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was Ibrahim Salkic with you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What about (redacted) ? Was he with you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, when asked by the Prosecutor, you did not deny the fact that in June of 1992, Tadic came to the elementary school and called all of you balijas and Ustasha. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You confirmed that fact?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And during your examination-in-chief, and in your statements, you said that Miroslav Tadic came to the elementary school only when there were exchanges taking place. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, do you know that there wasn't a single exchange in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you I wasn't sure. I don't know whether there was an exchange or not. If there wasn't one in June, then there must have been one in July. You're asking me now to remember some things that happened many years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: All I'm asking you is whether you remember that.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you to specify the time frame, and this is what you said, so all I'm interested in is whether you are still upholding that.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not specify the time period for the Prosecutor either. Perhaps there was some misunderstanding. I can't remember the time period now, in view of this ten-year gap.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember saying to the Prosecutor that Tadic came to the elementary school building on a number of occasions?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, and it was that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, do you know that while you were in the elementary school there were only two exchanges. One was on the 4th of July and the other one was on the 14th of August, 1992. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I know that there was more than 60 of us in the elementary school and that some 26, 27 people remained, who were later transferred to the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible -- could it be possible that Mr. Tadic came only on two occasions?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came on more than two occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When Miroslav Tadic came, there were other prisoners there with you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when he called you Ustashas and balijas, the others were able to hear that, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody who was there could hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And what other people were around you when Tadic called you, allegedly, Ustashas and balijas?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you read a list of people who were there with me, so you must know who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These people whose names I read out, meaning Hasan Bicic and the others, were able to hear what Miroslav Tadic said, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the representatives of the Red Cross came with him, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether that was on that occasion when he came with the Red Cross or on a later occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transcript does not reflect what the witness said. When I asked the witness whether the others who were there were able to hear what Miroslav Tadic said, the witness said "probably." So I will ask the witness to repeat the answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When I told you that Miroslav Tadic called you Ustashas and balijas, were other people able to hear what he said?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I replied by saying, "Probably, yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, I will read out to you an excerpt from your statement given on the 25th of April and 3rd of May, 1998, and it pertains to this visit of Miroslav Tadic. "Sometime during June of 1992, Miroslav Tadic came to the elementary school. He entered the gym where we were detained. Tadic came together with some people from the Serbian Red Cross in Bosanski Samac." Do you remember stating that, especially this bit, where it says that Tadic came together with the Red Cross people from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said, that he came with the Red Cross people. But at the time I didn't say that he used derogatory terms for us on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will continue reading on to you. You said that: "I know they represented the Red Cross because they had armbands indicating so. He introduced himself by saying that he was in charge of the exchanges. I saw that he brought a list of names. Both Croatian and Muslim names were on his list. Tadic called us all Ustashas." Here, in your statement, it says that on that occasion, in June 1992, Miroslav Tadic, in the presence of the Red Cross people, insulted you and called you all Ustashas and balijas. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if that's what it says in my 1998 statement, then it must be true. That's an official statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So that took place in June 1992, when he came with the Red Cross representatives?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly what month it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me: Those were representatives of the local Red Cross from Bosanski Samac, those people that came with Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the local Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were there women among them?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, after that, make any comments about Tadic's visit and the derogatory terms he used with respect to you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we probably did, but I don't remember any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that Tadic talked to some prisoners. Do you remember which prisoners he talked to?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you tell me when, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, then, on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. What is he referring to? Is he referring to -- are we now at the Batkovici or are we ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I suppose we are still at the elementary school, where Mr. Tadic is alleged to have gone with the representatives of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where in his statement does he say he talked to people? That's what I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the transcript. I'm talking about the transcript, page 30 through page 31. That's the draft version of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did Tadic talk to any of the prisoners on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, I indicated that he didn't talk to anyone, that he just read out the names and then left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The thing -- the paper that you have in front of you is your statement that you gave in 1998?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could he identify where or what he's referring to where he claims that this witness indicated that this defendant spoke to certain people? I don't see it in our transcript here. We're only talking about two pages. Apparently he's looking -- I see no reference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- Or any indication of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I'm trying to do. I have listed in my notes that the witness did, in fact, state that. I'm trying to find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic. Can we move on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will go back to that issue later, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, you mentioned in your testimony an event that your mother told you about. In the statement given to the Prosecutor in 1998, you did not mention anything about the alleged conversation between your mother and Mr. Tadic, although you did describe, in quite some detail, all the things that you learned from your mother; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you gave your statement, she gave a statement the day before you did; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At that time you lived together?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. We lived together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You confirmed that you were with your mother when she gave a statement to the Prosecution a few days ago; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please say -- did you say yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So when the Prosecutor talked to you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Which statement is he talking about? Is he talking about the statement that just occurred, the interview, not the statement, the interview that occurred one week ago, or is he talking about the interview which occurred in 1998? I'm not certain, and I don't know if the witness is certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic. You didn't specify which meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're talking about the meeting with the Prosecutor that took place a few days ago with Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present there, but you were talking about the statement. My mother gave only one official statement, and that was in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you were there a few days ago when your mother gave a statement -- when your mother --

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We discussed that yesterday, and Mr. Weiner did clarify. I don't see why we keep going round and round and wasting time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness and counsel please speak one at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm going directly to my topic. I just wanted to lay a foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now I will read a portion from the notes. It's on page 4 of the Prosecutor's notes. [In English] [Previous translation continues]... indicated that in July she went to see Miroslav Tadic. [Interpretation] I will skip this part, and I will read the last sentence: [In English] "She asked if it was a guarantee to happen she paid him. He said that he could not guarantee it, as it was not only up to him. Since the defendant could not guarantee an exchange occurring, she decided not to pay one hundred and two thousand [sic] German marks to Tadic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Two corrections. One apparently my typing is not that good. She asked if it was guaranteed to happen. There should be the word "if." And the other thing is he said 1. -- Okay. 1.200 marks. I'm sorry. 1.200 German Deutschmarks. I thought he said 1,000 and 2 or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember saying that to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My mother said that. I was present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of July, you stated before this Trial Chamber that your mother, as she told you, gave up because she didn't have enough money. That was on page 73/23. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you must have heard from your mother that when she told you that Tadic told her that it was not up to him and that she -- that he -- she shouldn't give him any money?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, you are now twisting the facts. So she did not give up. She had no money. Is that the situation?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say that I'm twisting facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you say in your statement that your mother didn't want to give any money, that she couldn't get any guarantees? Then you said that she gave up because she apparently -- allegedly didn't have money.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there were any guarantees, my mother would have found the money somehow and would have given that money.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness and counsel please speak one at a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, can you wait for the witness. And the witness should also wait for counsel to complete the answer. The interpreters are having difficulties to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, is it correct that you stated yesterday that your mother didn't give money to Miroslav Tadic because she didn't have any? Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Why did she go to see Miroslav Tadic to offer him money that she didn't have?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a problem of money. Money would have been found in some way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So she gave up because she couldn't get any guarantees?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, when she -- that your mother told you that she was visiting Mr. Tadic, it was in the summer of 1992, an investigation was underway against you in the SUP and you were giving a statement. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave one statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, your wife and child were exchanged on the 7th of October, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes. Yes. I know that it was in October 1992, but I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Miroslav Tadic was present when they were exchanged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your wife didn't give any money to Miroslav Tadic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: She didn't offer him any money?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Miroslav Tadic didn't ask her for any money; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't ask for any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your mother was exchanged in June 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: She didn't offer any money to Miroslav Tadic to be exchanged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did Miroslav Tadic ask for any money from her, for her to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, in November you were transferred to the camp in Batkovici, and as you stated, you went there together with all those persons who were detained in the TO building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Omer Nalic, do you remember that he was also transferred with you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Kemal Mehinovic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Ibrahim Salkic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Abdulah Drljacic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in Batkovici representatives of the International Red Cross visited you.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that in November, when you were transferred there, you told them about the people who were detained in Zasavica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did the representatives of the International Red Cross let you know that they were familiar with the fact of what was going on in Zasavica in September, as early as in September?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know that we discussed it with them, but I don't know what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you, when you told them about Zasavica, that they had already spoken to Jelena Kapetanovic, as early as in the beginning of September 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I didn't hear you well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Do you know Jelena Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know her by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
