utterances.text: Did the representatives of the International Red Cross tell you that they spoke with people in Zasavica as early as in September and that specifically they talked to Jelena Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would object at this time for a few reasons. Number one, does he have a document by the Red Cross indicating that they were aware of the incident as early as September? Number two, was it the same people who spoke to Jelena Kapetanovic? Were they the same persons who spoke to these prisoners? Was there coordination between the two Red Cross groups? Unless -- if he has a document from the Red Cross, or if he is planning on bringing a Red Cross representative from the International Red Cross to testify, that's fair cross-examination, but if he isn't, I'd argue that that's improper cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wanted to ask the witness whether -- now, I don't know if the Prosecutor had the document about the visit of the International Red Cross to Batkovici when he asked the questions of this witness. I didn't ask about any documents; I merely asked about facts. Because now the Prosecutor is trying to introduce the statement that the people in Zasavica were being concealed, that there were attempts to keep it under cover and that the people from the Red Cross were informed about Zasavica only in November from the prisoners in Batkovici, and that's the line of questioning that the Prosecutor is doing. Because we -- and that's wrong, because we had Jelena Kapetanovic as a witness here, who confirmed that, as early as in August and September 1992, representatives of the International Red Cross were already in Zasavica. So I'm not asking about any documents; I'm asking about the fact whether he was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. If you want to know even the Territorial Defence was registered, but we were imprisoned there, and only two or three men were shown, and the rest of us were kept under cover. And if you were to ask these people, they would tell you that they were registered as early as in September 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner --

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Jelena Kapetanovic also could have been the one that was shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just going to say that counsel indicated August/September Jelena Kapetanovic's testimony was sometime in October, sometime in October, so that's a misquote of her testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: She said that the Red Cross visited them in October or --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes around the 5th of October, she says.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. And that they were taken there in August, so they had been there for some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At any rate, it was before the transfer of the prisoners to Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, yesterday you said, on page 45, that you saw Miroslav Tadic for the first time in Batkovici in January, in 1993.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How often did Miroslav Tadic come to Batkovici from January 1993 onwards?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. I don't know. Whenever there was an exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Two, three, four, five times?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you with any certainty, but he did come on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw him in Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As regards your going to Bijeljina for the trial, did you see him after that time?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: When Miroslav Tadic came to the elementary school building, did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether he had a beard in the elementary school, but I remember that he had a beard in Batkovici. That I can confirm with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, when you saw him then, did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not have a beard at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How was he dressed when he came to the elementary school building?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he wore civilian clothes, but I can't tell you with full certainty. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember: When was (redacted), exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when the exchanges in Batkovici took place?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me to furnish information that is ten years old. I really can't give you an answer to that. It's not that I can't, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you are a fact witness here, and I noticed that your memory doesn't fail you when you answer Prosecutor's questions. So I suppose that we are now covering the same events?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is not correct. There are many times the witness said he couldn't remember, especially the dates, and some facts he didn't remember. So it's not correct to say that. Just go on with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, yesterday you described an incident involving Sabah Seric and the time when he went to be exchanged. Please tell me: There was just one person with the last name of Seric with you in Batkovici? That was the only person from Samac with that last name; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, the only person?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I mean: The only person with that last name Seric.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the last name or the first name as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the first and the last name.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was there another Seric with you in Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We didn't get interpretation of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How old is Sabah Seric?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean now or then?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Then. How old was he then?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was probably born either in 1954 or in 1956, around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know his father's name?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When Seric was exchanged, do you remember who called out the names of the people to be exchanged? Was it Miroslav Tadic or one of the guards?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. All I remember is that Miroslav Tadic came with the lists, and as to who read out the names, I really don't know. Probably him, but I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when was this business with the lists taking place? Where was it taking place? Was it in the hangar or in the yard?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It was in that fence-in part of the prison in Batkovici, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you say "hangar," you must know what "hangar" means. That was your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Did Sabah Seric tell you that he paid, gave money, to Miroslav Tadic in order to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw that, and he also told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you saw that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that, as did others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see exactly?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the lists were read out, some of the persons were not present, and then Sabah went up to Miroslav Tadic, put money into his hand. Miroslav Tadic went out, and later on came back with corrected lists and read out Sabah Seric's name, who was later exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he give the money into -- did he put the money into his hand?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that moment when the money was exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how -- what it looked like? Did he put the money into his hand?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know how it is when money is given and accepted; it's just clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is the Defence disputing that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then we don't need to go into all those details. You can simply contradict the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since the witness did not reply to my question directly when I asked him whether he saw Sabah Seric give money to Miroslav Tadic, he said "probably," and then, faced with my other question, he said, "Well, you know how it is when money is exchanged."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So based on that, sir, I'm concluding that you did not see, yourself, the moment when Sabah Seric gave money to Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see that, but now you are asking me to remember in detail things that happened ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't remember all of the details regarding this?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite naturally, I can't remember all of the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That he put the money into his hands?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember him giving the money to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: You probably stood nearby and must have heard the conversation that preceded that scene?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard the conversation that preceded that scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe that conversation?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sabah asked Miroslav what -- saying that he will give him money for himself and for another person; however, Miroslav Tadic refused to accept money for Muris Mehic but accepted money only for Sabah, and Sabah was later exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How long was that conversation?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps five minutes, three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were any of your fellow citizens nearby as well?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Muris Mehic, others whose names I can't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will now read the names of some of the witnesses, and therefore I will ask that we now turn to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Some of them are protected witnesses. All right. Can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then immediately thereafter, Seric was exchanged; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This event took place before your trial in Bijeljina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably is right, but I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long before your trial in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean where I went from Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No. I mean the trial in Bijeljina. Can you tell me: In relation to your trial in Bijeljina, when did this event with Sabah Seric take place?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in January 1993, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Some other fellow citizens of yours were exchanged together with Sabah Seric, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that Avdo Drljacic and (redacted) were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This affair with Sabah Seric giving money for his exchange is something that you didn't mention to the Prosecutor when you talked to them in 1998; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably because nobody asked me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to put on the ELMO a list for exchange so that the witness could take a look at it. It's an Exhibit P25/3 -- or rather, D25/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, can you see this document?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the date in the upper-left corner?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, what are you trying to establish through this list?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is the list of people exchanged in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The exchange in which Mr. Sabah Seric was included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 24th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the witness is claiming that that took place sometime between January 1993 and the summer of 1993. So I would like the witness to take a look at the date of this list and to see whether Mr. Seric is on this list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness didn't claim anything. I simply said that I thought it was in January of 1993. So it means that I was wrong by just one month. I'm telling you again: It's been ten years since that time, and you're asking me about the dates. I can tell you when I was exchanged. I was exchanged on the 9th of June, 1994. Don't ask me about the dates of other exchanges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just going to suggest, so we can move this along, rather than have the witness read it, could we just read it out to the witness? Because I don't know if he can see what we've got and I don't know if he can see what he's got --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Does the Prosecution have this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, we have the document. I just thought to move it along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. What number is the name you are dealing with, you want, Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can the Prosecutor look at number 24?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. I see it right here. If he can just read it out to the witness, that's fine. I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, what you're seeing now is the list of people exchanged on the 24th of December, 1992, people exchanged in Dragalic, and under number 24 you can see the name of Seric Sabah, son of Hasan, or rather, it's a bit unclear here. Do you remember whether this person listed under number 24 is the person we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you have trouble reading the name of that person, then how do you expect me to read his name? You told me that the name is written not clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, it's your case, but that name under that number is the person you are talking about, the one who, according to this witness, paid the money. So you simply tell the witness that according to this list, dated whatever, it shows that this person was exchanged on this date. That's all. Because, after all, the witness has said that he cannot remember other exchanges, the dates of other exchanges; he can only remember his own exchange. So I don't even see how material this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, are you still claiming that Miroslav Tadic came to Batkovici for the first time in January 1993, as you said a number of times here before this Tribunal and in your statements?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I don't remember with full certainty. It could be that he came for the first time in January of 1993, because there was one exchange in Batkovici in January of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, Sabah Seric was exchanged in December of 1992, and it was impossible for you to witness this event in January of 1993; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I told you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us briefly. Are you still upholding your previous claim?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm still upholding my previous statement that I don't remember when did this take place exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Subasic, I wonder whether you could tell me -- I'm not that familiar with surnames from the former Yugoslavia, but I wonder whether you could tell me: Is this surname Seric a popular -- a fairly popular name, like Smith or Jones would be in the United States, let's say? Is it a name where there could have been perhaps more than one Seric in the camp in Batkovici? Please, it would be of assistance if you could clarify this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Seric family has many members in Bosanski Samac. It could be that there was another person with the last name of Seric in the camp, but I can't tell you with certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, in your testimony, or rather, in your statement given to the Prosecutor, pages 43, 44, you described how you went to the military court in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What testimony or what statement are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony yesterday.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How many times were you taken to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think twice, once to be interrogated and then for the sentencing - the so-called sentencing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You told the Prosecutor that you had been in some kind of an office, the place that looked like an office?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the interrogation, there were other people present there apart from you in the office; is that true?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Boro Pisarevic, Goran Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The typist was also there who took down your statement. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned that the lawyer, the judge, and the typist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The lawyer was not our colleague Mr. Pisarevic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I saw him in the courtroom when we were brought in. I don't know whether he had anything to do with our case, but it was like as if -- it seemed that I had seen him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did the investigative judge, in the course of your interrogation, tell you what you are charged with, what criminal offences? Did he mention the armed insurrection or something like that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He asked me if I participated in the night guards in Samac, if I had any weapons in Samac, if I was a member of the SDA, if I was a member of any other party, and then in the end, when I received the statement, none of the questions were listed there, and the only thing that was stated there was that pursuant to Article this and that of the law of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: All right. We'll come to that. Let me just ask you a few preliminary questions. Did you receive the decree about the assignment of counsel, ex officio?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did. I don't remember. But I did have a defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did the investigating judge or the defence counsel tell you that without the interview with the investigative judge, according to the Criminal Code -- code on law and criminal procedure that --

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please tell me: What law are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you whether they told you that.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did, and they did quote the law. I don't remember the exact article, but I do remember that it was such-and-such law of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated] I apologise. I have problems with my microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So they did mention to you, they did note the article of the Criminal Code and the criminal offence that you were being charged with; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. The criminal offence was armed insurrection or armed rebellion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did the investigating judge or the lawyer tell you that according to the law in force at that time it was not allowed to consult the defence counsel before being questioned by the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. Can you please tell me: Which law was in force at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will answer your question, but I would like to clear this up. I'm aware that you're familiar with the law, and you probably are familiar with the fact that we in the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that we -- that the laws of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia were used to prosecute us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, just wait for the questions from counsel. Do not ask counsel any questions. Just answer the questions put to you by counsel. If you don't know, you say so. Do not ask counsel any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Subasic, did the investigating judge tell you that during the interrogation of the accused in front of the investigative judge that the accused is not confronted with the statements of the witness, of any witnesses?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing was told to us. Nobody asked us anything there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the questioning in front of the investigating judge, did you sign any statements?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did sign a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the Prosecutor on the 3rd of May - and you repeated that on page 43 of the transcript yesterday - that the statement was completely different from the one that you gave and that the facts were twisted and changed. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me: Which facts were changed and twisted?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just beginning to tell you. When I came there and when he started to ask me questions whether I had weapons, whether I was a member of the SDA party, of the HDZ party, whether I took part in the night guards in Bosanski Samac, and I told him that I did nothing of the above. I was not a member of any party. I didn't take part in any protests or any guard duty. They let me go out of the office. I went back to Batkovici. And then a few days later I was brought back there and then an indictment was read to me, indicating that I was charged with armed rebellion, pursuant to such-and-such article of the Criminal Code of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you did read and you did sign the statement given in front of the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that statement was not changed. You merely received an indictment -- a new document?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed my statement, but the statement that came back to me was something completely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What was that something, this other thing that you were given?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the statement, the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you were given the indictment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So not your statement that you had signed, but the indictment signed by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably I was charged in accordance with the statement that I had given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did the judge ask you to plead guilty or not guilty for the criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And how did you plead?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I plead not guilty. I can't see what I had to feel guilty for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me: Did you receive the judgement after the trial?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And for which criminal offence were you convicted?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was convicted of armed rebellion in the territory of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what was the sentence?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twelve years in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you appeal against the judgement?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Appeal to whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you write an appeal challenging the judgement?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't write any appeals. I didn't appeal to anyone. And do you want me to tell you why?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were there like cattle. Nobody asked us anything. And our lives were in danger every day. We were brought to the courtroom in a truck, like cattle. We were made to run out into the yard. We had to face the wall. We didn't know where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, let me ask you something. Did the investigating judge ask you anything about Dedo Halilovic, your neighbour?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, your neighbour, Dedo Halilovic, was a high-ranking official of the Party of Democratic Action in Bosanski Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, because I was not a member of that party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your neighbour Dedo Halilovic was also the commander of the engineer section of the armed unit that was made up of Muslims. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your neighbour Dedo Halilovic --

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, can you tell me where? Where was he the commander of that unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In Samac.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your neighbour Dedo Halilovic was one of the organisers of the barricades or roadblocks that were set up by the SDA in Samac. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. As I already said, I never took part in any protests, any barricades.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your neighbour Dedo Halilovic took part in the distribution of illegal weapons in Bosanski Samac. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your neighbour Dedo Halilovic gave you an automatic pistol and three clips of ammunition on the 15th of April, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I never had any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Between the 16th and the 17th of April, and the 17th and 18th of April, on those two nights, you took part in the fighting in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Could you please tell me: What was the fighting that was going on in Bosanski Samac? How many people were killed there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That submachine-gun and the three clips of ammunition that you obtained, you took them to your uncle's house, Galib Nurkic. That's your uncle. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you hid the weapons in his basement?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Galib did not have a basement in his house. So if you want to hear the details, and if you're asking the questions that I -- about the facts that I hear for the first time, Galib Nurkic's house did not have a basement at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was a rifle found at your uncle's place, Galib Nurkic's place, that he handed over to the authorities?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Subasic, that in the document that you received from the military court in Bijeljina, that the facts that I just -- the factual allegations that I just mentioned are quoted in there?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you have that document with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please show that document to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We received it only today. It's a very bad copy, hardly legible. We will put it on the ELMO, and perhaps I could read it to you and then the interpreters can confirm.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like you to read to me, read out the article of the relevant law and the relevant state where that law was in force, according to which I was convicted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, since you're saying that your copies are very bad, I don't know how you intend to use them. Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This afternoon we received three documents. None of them are indictments. These are documents -- one is three years after the fact, relating to the charges; one concerns that the persons have been interviewed and that further investigations should occur; and the other basically says that further investigations should occur. But unless he has an indictment -- counsel just indicated that they have this indictment. I haven't seen it. Do they have another document that we haven't seen? Also, I haven't seen a copy of any statement that this witness has given. Where is the statement, so we can make a comparison if they received these documents, where are the rest of the package of documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may explain. In his testimony, this witness -- the witness indicated that in 1993 he was sentenced to 12 years in prison. Our investigators went to the files, to the archives of the military court in Bijeljina, and in the registry of judgements. They did not find the judgement and they did not find the indictment pursuant to which this witness would be sentenced to 12 years in prison. Our investigators, in the course of his testimony, went to the archives of the Prosecutor's office and found the three documents that we received today by fax, and we immediately disclosed them to the Prosecutor. One is the request -- is the decree to initiate an investigation, indicating quite clearly what the accused is charged with, the criminal offence that he is charged with and the decree --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the document dated 9th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is dated 15th of May, 1993. That's the proposal of the public prosecutor for additional investigation to be conducted. And the next document is the decision on the abolishment of the criminal proceedings against this witness. It was issued by the investigating judge and it was dated 12th of September, 1995, which would mean that no indictment was ever issued against this witness and that he was never sentenced to 12 years in prison. But the documents that the witness stated that he did receive some of them clearly indicate the factual allegations and the charges against him, the criminal offences that he is charged with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Number one, the document relating to what appears to be a dismissal of charges is September 12th, it looks like 1996 on mine. Part of these documents are illegible, but it appears to be 1996, so over three years later. The document dated the 15th of May is -- it must be a form, because it's in two different typewriters or two different types of typewriting. And the third document is apparently from the initial interview, dated May -- it appears -- I'm sorry. April 9th, 1993. Counsel have had notice of this witness testifying in relation to this incident since 1998, 1999, at least April of 1999, and these just show up today. These are not statements of this particular witness. These are not direct statements of this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I think the best way is for you to deal with it in your defence when you've got documents that can be read, you can just put what your case is to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it was not my intention to read these documents. We disclosed them to the Prosecutor as soon as we received them. We just wanted to ask this witness about some facts. So I don't want to tender them into evidence at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Subasic, you did receive the decision on the initiation of the investigation. Was this the decision that you received, or was that the judgement that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the judgement. I would like to ask a question to you. You didn't answer my question. Could I ask the Court's permission for you to give me the answer to that question, and that will clarify a lot of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which question do you want the counsel to answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is whether in these documents that the Defence counsel produced now, is there the article and the law quoted there under which the investigation against me was initiated? Do these documents reflect that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The counsel has said that he doesn't wish to have these documents produced. He is not going to use them. So he can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you will allow me, I could read this out to the witness, because it's stated quite clearly in here. If the Trial Chamber would allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is stated there? The charge?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It gives the article of the law under which this witness was charged. Your Honours, specifically, this is the crime of armed insurrection, under Article 124(1) and Article 139(3) of the adopted law on Criminal Code of Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, Your Honour, the document dated April 4th, 1993 refers to Article 139 of the Socialist Republic of Yugoslavia. However, once again for the record, the document dated September 1996 refers to Article 139 of the Republic of Srpska that he was charged with. And the third document, just says Article 139. It doesn't state -- 124 and Article 139, but it doesn't state which republic or which nation the laws emanate from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you will just allow me to clarify this for my colleague from the Prosecution. In view of the fact that the former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia had ceased to exist, the countries that stemmed from it passed the decision on adopting certain formal laws of the SFRY, and the Criminal Code of that country was adopted both by Republika Srpska and the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And later on, when this other document was issued, at that time Republika Srpska had already adopted its own Criminal Code. So therefore, that Criminal Code was applied on the territory of the entire Bosnia and Herzegovina at that time, but later on we will discuss this in our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. There is no need for us to go on with this debate. Please move on, Mr. Krgovic. We've had enough on what he was charged with. He himself had earlier mentioned that it was armed insurrection, so we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Subasic, you never received the judgement sentencing you to 12 years' imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So therefore, you never received the judgement sentencing you to 12 years of imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I received the judgement, but I never had to serve that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And was the judgement perhaps publicly read out to you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was given the judgement at the court in Bijeljina. It was read out to me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And was it actually -- this document that I just read out to you, that's the document that you received; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I was just going to say the same thing. You just read out the articles from the particular criminal codes, but the witness hasn't seen the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will move on from this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: You were exchanged in Satorovici in 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't see Miroslav Tadic at that location where you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Nor did he come to fetch you in Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a correction for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You did not see Miroslav Tadic at the location of your exchange?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You went to exchange, together with Izet Ramusovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Esad Dzakic and Mirsad Srna went there with you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And according to you, you were still under that sentence, sentencing you to 12 years' imprisonment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if the sentence was passed down in 1993 and I was exchanged in 1994, then yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lazarevic, how much time do you think you'll need?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do believe I can complete my cross-examination in one hour, maybe 10, 15 minutes more, but it depends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. You can start.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one matter. If he can complete it in one hour, is there a possibility of going beyond 7.00 tonight? I only have five minutes of re-direct at this time, so we can finish it tonight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let's start now and see how we move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Are we going to take a break in two minutes or not? I just need to ... [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe we shall forfeit our break and simply go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Subasic. My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic. I'm the Defence counsel representing Mr. Zaric in this case. I will be cross-examining you. Before I commence my cross-examination, I would like to tell you that my client would like to express his regret for everything that you and your family suffered during the wartime in Bosnia. My client has asked me to convey this to you. But before I start asking my questions, let me please tell you: Since I have observed that sometimes there is some overlapping between questions and answers, I would like to ask you to wait briefly before answering my questions, because the interpreters are warning us here that they are unable to follow this pace of examination. So please make a brief pause before giving your answers. Let me start with this: In your statement here before this Tribunal, you spoke about some rallies that were held before the 17th of April, and also you spoke about the gathering of citizens which took place after the accident at the Valentino cafe. Do you remember talking about that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You were present at that gathering; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sulejman Tihic, the then president of the SDA in Bosanski Samac, spoke at that rally; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember who gave speeches. I know that there were a lot of people there, but I couldn't tell you with certainty who gave speeches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I'm sorry. I was reminded by the registry assistant that the interpreters do need a break, because they do get exhausted. So I'm afraid we shall have to take our 20-minutes' break and resume at 10 minutes before 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic. You're continuing cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Subasic, we left it off at that rally which was held after the accident in the Valentino Cafe. I have just one more question: Do you remember Simo Zaric speaking at that rally?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. In that case, we'll move on to another topic, then. The Prosecutor asked you certain things about the 4th Detachment. You said that you knew its members well. And I would like to ask you a few things about the 4th Detachment now. Do you know when it was founded?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the 4th Detachment was within the JNA?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Does the name 17th Tactical Group mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Radovan Antic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was the commander of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know somebody called Jovo Savic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know that man?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was the zone of responsibility of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many members the 4th Detachment had?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Prior to the 17th of April, 1992, have you seen members of the 4th Detachment in uniforms and armed?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them armed. I didn't see them in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you see them walking about the town of Samac with their arms, or how did you see them?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw some of the members in Samac armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you give me the names of these people?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, Goran Cicic, Damir Ibralic, Fadil Topcagic, Denis Topcagic. And I couldn't really give you any other names. I've truly forgotten them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When did you see them walking about the town of Samac armed?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them together as a group. I would see them individually, in various cafes, armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These people that you just mentioned, all of them are Muslims, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Who isn't?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Goran Cicic, Damir Ibralic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You never saw the list of the members of the 4th Detachment, have you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you never saw the entire 4th Detachment lined up; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you saw the entire 4th Detachment lined up?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now let's turn to another topic, involving the events of the 17th of April, 1992. You already replied to the questions put to you by Mr. Krgovic, and I will try to avoid repeating these questions, but there are certain details that need to be clarified. On the 17th of April, 1992, in the morning, around 7.00, were you together with your uncle, Galib Nurkic? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you hiding in his house?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had nobody to hide from. I simply came there, spent a brief amount of time there, and went back to my apartment, just as I've told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did your mother come to your uncle's house on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. When I came to the apartment, my mother wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that it was precisely your uncle, Galib Nurkic, who told your mother that you were with him in his apartment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know about that. How could I know about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, yesterday counsel for Miroslav Tadic asked some questions in relation to an interview that this witness's mother had given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And we had some disagreement between two counsel as to whether or not such testimony was admissible. This witness testified that maybe the statement that she gave, maybe his mother got it wrong or it was recorded incorrectly. I have the statement in front of me, and the statement, as I told you yesterday, was given on the 2nd of May, and it says 1950, which I believe is probably 1998. It's incorrect. However, on the last page of the statement, it says: "This statement was not reread to the witness," meaning this witness's mother, "and therefore, the witness has not had an opportunity to verify or acknowledge the accuracy and truth of the statement." So what Defence counsel is doing is they're attempting to impeach this witness, that's on the stand now, with statements based on an interview from this witness's mother, which have never been verified or have never been reviewed or reread by the witness. So we don't even know if this is an accurate statement. As a result, I'd argue, based on our policy in this case of using one witness to impeach another witness, unless it's done directly from the witness stand, I'd request that such questioning cease at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I remember correctly my own words, I never said, not in one word, that I was using his mother's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe this is the conclusion that my learned friend has, but I never impeached the witness through his mother's statement. I never asked him to comment on his mother's statement. I'm asking him about certain facts. And this is not only his mother's statement that is the source of our informations. We also have some other informations, and in due course I will tell this witness where these informations come from. So I don't think that this objection has any basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Weiner, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, we have certain information. You have just now heard what the Prosecutor said, and I will not refer to your mother's statement, but however, we have other sources of information, and I will now present that to you. The questions are quite simple. You can give us yes or no answers or you can say that you don't remember. So we left it off at that spot where we spoke about your uncle, Galib Nurkic, and the fact that you spent the entire 17th of April hiding in his house, that your mother came, that she talked to you, and that you told her that you did not dare go back home because you had heard that Serbs were going around Samac arresting people. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did your uncle, Galib Nurkic, visit Bosanski Samac last year?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was last year. I can't remember whether it was the last year or the year before the last. It could be the one before the last.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that what I just told you is something that your uncle, Galib Nurkic, said in front of a number of citizens of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you have that written out and signed by him?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, we are back again. Please answer the questions put to you by counsel. Do not ask counsel any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that your uncle, Galib Nurkic, stated this in the presence of a large number of residents of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, and I don't believe that he stated something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that your uncle stated this in front of Ratko Tubakovic and Lazo Markovic, called Devetka, would that help you refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could that refresh my memory if I wasn't present there? I left Samac in 1992 and never returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, let's go back to April of 1992. You knew that your uncle had an automatic weapon called Kalashnikov; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he had what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That your uncle, Galib Nurkic, had that.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that he was given that weapon by the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that, and I don't believe that he could receive that from the party, because he was never a member of that party.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the SDA party kept a record of weapons issued?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably did, but since I wasn't a member, I don't know about their records and how they kept them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, in your testimony before this Tribunal, you said that on the 17th of April, at around 8.00 a.m. - this is the way I understood it - that you saw your very good friend Esad Dagovic at a distance of about 20 to 30 metres from his home. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Apart from Mr. Esad Dagovic, did you on that occasion see Hasan Bicic, nicknamed Hasa?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you a question about a certain number of names, and could you please say if you saw them or not. So just reply with yes or no. Nusret Kapetanovic? Did you see Nusret Kapetanovic too?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that person. I really don't know who he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Suad Dujmonic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Damir Dzakic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Ferhat Sahacic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Muharem Drljacic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who that person is at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you don't know who that person is, please say so. Mirsad Srna.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Salko Srna?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him. I don't remember seeing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Muharem Jasarevic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Suad Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fadil Sabanovic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Osman Mesic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him. When I say I don't know those persons, that would mean that I simply perhaps don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Ratif Atic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Kemal Atic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your neighbour, Dervis Halilovic, nicknamed Dedo?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What about Kemal Mehinovic, the baker, Kemal?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Izet Ramusovic, Haso?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Muhamed Bicic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Hasan's brother, Muhamed Bicic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Safet Dagovic, Esad's brother?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see Safet either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What about Ibrahim Salkic, Ibela?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've already asked me about him. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you about Pasaga Tihic, if you saw him then?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So on that occasion, at around 8.00 a.m. on the 17th of April, you saw only Esad Dagovic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to enumerate all the people that I saw?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sure. It would be of great help.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Markica Nogic, Ivica Stipo, Kajo, Marko Dzemal [phoen], Tubakovic, Rizo. I can't remember his last name, but he had the cafe called Cardak. You probably know the person I'm talking about. My next-door neighbours Husic Cicko, Zijad, Goran Mamuzic, Nikisa Boro Palisnica [phoen]. That's as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can see here that your memory is quite good, but in your statement you mentioned only Esad Dagovic, and this is the first time that you mentioned this, when I'm asking you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, you have to assume, number one, that he was questioned concerning all these different people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I will go the other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Subasic, you already gave this statement to the Prosecutors. We have this statement here before us and you also have it before you. That's the statement dated the 25th of April and the 3rd of May, 1998. In that statement you did not mention Esad Dagovic at all. If you can check -- if you want to check it, you can do so, because you have the statement before you. So if you find Esad Dagovic, please let me know, because I was unable to find his name.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mention him because at that time nobody asked me about him. Nobody asked me about the other people either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, on the 17th of April, in the early morning, did you see any Muslims from your town that were armed?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: According to our information, sir, you spent the entire day of the 17th outside of your apartment, and it was only on the 18th of April, in the morning, that you returned to your apartment. Can you please confirm that fact? Or do you still maintain that on the 17th of April, in the morning, you were in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When in the morning? Because I said that I was out between 6.30 and 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. That you were in your apartment after 8.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on now to the event when the soldiers came to your apartment to gather weapons. You said that this happened on the 17th of April. Could you please look at your statement, on page 3 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: For the benefit of my colleagues from the Prosecution, it's page 2, first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The next morning, when I looked out of my window, I saw many soldiers going from house to house." Do you still maintain this?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So this is happening on the 17th, in the morning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No, not in the morning; in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, there is a very big difference between "in the morning" and "in the afternoon." In your statement, it says: "The next morning, when I looked out of my window, I saw many soldiers." Do you want to amend your testimony?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object to that.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just want to tell you once again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, when he testified in direct, we said either the morning or the afternoon was the question that was asked to him. He wasn't clear. He thought it was the afternoon, but he just wasn't sure. There's no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The time when he saw the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct. In his statement, he does say the morning; however, when he did testify here, he's indicated morning or afternoon. He's not that certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: In fact, I think, Mr. Weiner, if my memory serves me correctly, yesterday he said late morning or afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Late morning. That's what I found in transcript, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you then tell us whether it was at around 9.00 or at around 7.00 or 8.00 in the evening? And let me remind you: We are in the month of April and the days are short.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact time when this happened because, after all, more than ten years have passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Before the soldiers appeared, how long had you been in the house? Because you said that you had returned home at around 8.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several hours perhaps, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Would that be an hour or two hours?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you can't remember. Of course. You said in your statement that Zaric and Tadic were in a military vehicle. It was quite unclear to me, in fact, so could you please clarify what kind of a military vehicle it was? Was it a car that was used by military? Was it a jeep? Was it a self-propelled vehicle? Was it a tank. Could you please tell me, what was it?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was some kind of a personnel carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. It was a personnel carrier. Were Zaric and Tadic sitting inside or outside of the carrier?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was some kind of a pinzgauer vehicle. They were standing on the vehicle at the time when I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So they were standing on the vehicle that was open, that was roofless, and I suppose that there was some kind of a canvas cover, if it was possible to open it that way?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Where were the other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your entrance in that building, in Edvarda Kardelja Street, is the first entrance?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, when Zaric and Tadic allegedly came, which other neighbours of yours were present there, I mean those from your entrance, entrance number 1?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Dr. Ruza was there, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think so too. And as regards this lady doctor by the name of Ruza, that would be Ruza Brdar Masic; that's her full name. When we talk about her, she is a relative of your wife, Vera?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The reason why I'm asking you this is because on several occasions your personal details indicate that a doctor who lives in the same building, in the same entrance as you do, is a relative of your wife, so I just wanted to clarify whether this is Dr. Ruza Brdar Masic.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the doctor, but I don't know whether she is related to my wife or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I will not belabour this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, where in the statement does -- is that indicated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He just stated that your personal details indicated on several occasions that Dr. Ruza was a relative of your wife, and I'm asking where in the statement is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will have that in a very short moment, because I have a lot of statements here. Maybe this was not his statement, maybe it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's not his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On some other witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Some other witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- what we do is compare some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. I didn't really want to mislead. I just needed the information if this --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- person is in family relationship with his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Let's continue where we left off. When the weapons were collected, was your mother in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So at that time, when, according to your testimony, Messrs. Tadic and Zaric entered the building with a number of soldiers, she was in the apartment

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was not your mother at the market at that time, where she wanted to buy eggs, and that she, in fact, returned when everything was over?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about the market, but what time are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the time when the event concerning the collection of weapons in the building number 64 Edvarda Kardelja Street, entrance number 1, at that time when Zaric and Tadic allegedly were in the building together with several soldiers, is it true that your mother was on the market at the time to buy eggs and that she returned later, when everything was over?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This probably isn't correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Before this Trial Chamber, you said that, apart from Zaric and Tadic, there were between 10 and 15 soldiers there. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me the names of the soldiers that were there at the time with Tadic and Zaric, as you say?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you, because I don't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember at least one name out of the 10 or 15?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you were to refresh my memory, because you did the same thing a little while ago when you mentioned the persons relating to my uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But did you personally know any of the 10 or 15 soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe, but I don't remember their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course, if you can't remember, you can't remember. On that occasion, was the apartment of Dr. Ruza Brdar searched? You said you were there. Do you remember if her apartment was searched?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. I think that they only entered the apartment and had a very quick perfunctory look. They didn't really search.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this event, we have totally different information from the information contained in your testimony. According to our information, neither Mr. Zaric nor Mr. Tadic, nor any of the soldiers, entered the apartment where you lived; quite the contrary. One of the soldiers rang your bell, asked you for a glass of water, you gave him a glass of water, and that's all that happened as part of that incident. Is our information correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's possible that the soldier had a drink of water when he got in. My apartment was not searched as thoroughly as Dedo's apartment. They didn't break anything, they didn't take anything. They asked me if I had any weapons. I said I didn't. So it was just talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You don't really consider that to be an incident at all?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is an incident if you have five or six armed people enter your apartment where your little child is. It would qualify as an incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you depict this entire incident as you -- did you tell your mother when she came home from the market, when everything was over, did you tell her that a soldier merely asked you for a glass of water and that you gave him a glass of water? Is this what you said to your mother?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
