utterances.text: My mother was --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Number one, how is it relevant what conversation he had with his mother?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What is the relevance of what conversation he had with his mother?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can explain that, Your Honour. I mean, we are using all possible evidence that we can. All the informations that we have, and our colleague from the Prosecution are aware where we got this information from.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The thing is that it has relevance, of course, that if this witness spoke with his mother, and about the incident, where he said that allegedly five soldiers came inside his -- and scared his children and everything, and if he says to his mother, "Mother, nothing actually happened. There was one soldier asking for a glass of water," then we do believe that it is relevant for our case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, when I objected previously concerning impeaching this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. You are thinking that the source of his information is the statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He just said: You know where I got this statement. It's right here. This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I said that. I said to my colleague of the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He said, "You know where I got this statement."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I never stated this to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's using is it. You can't do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You know the objection of the Prosecution, and please do not repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Unless in your Defence case you are going to call a witness who perhaps was present --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Your Honours, I cannot be 100 per cent certain if I am going to call one of the witnesses, because, you see, we did have certain problems about approaching ex-Prosecution witnesses, and at this moment I cannot be 100 per cent of that. Because I'm going to have to go through Prosecution or some other way to get these witnesses. I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Do be honest that you are not using the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did Dr. Brdar Masic, who you say was present there, was she in the corridor and was she able to observe everything that was going on?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even if she had been in the corridor, I don't remember where she was, because Dr. Ruza lived on one floor below us, and I don't really know where she was. So she wouldn't have been able to see us anyway. Later on I realised -- I saw that she was at home and she came up to see us and we talked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you don't remember. But sir, on the 17th of April, my client, Mr. Simo Zaric, was not in Samac at all. He was in Pelagicevo. Do you perhaps allow that this may have been some other day?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer. We didn't hear him very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness's answer wasn't picked up by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, actually, he said: "I don't remember that well," I think. We have his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure whether we heard it correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I didn't say "I don't remember." I said I did not want to change my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. The record will be amended accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe his answer is now recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. We're back on the 17th in the morning hours. You said in your testimony that you didn't notice anything peculiar in the town apart from the fact that some soldiers were in the Cafe AS. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in front of the Cafe AS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, but I don't remember -- but I did know more or less all of them, but I can't now give you the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. I will not insist. Just one more question. Your grandmother, she died in December 1993, if my information is correct. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: She had a kidney disease; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Throughout 1992, and up until the time when she died in 1993, she underwent dialysis in Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes, but I can't tell you with any certainty because I was imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: She is of Muslim ethnicity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to move on to another topic, and that's your transfer from the TO building to the military barracks in Brcko. Can you please tell me whether that took place on the 26th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the night of the 26th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At that time, when the two military trucks, together with the military police officers, came in, were you inside the TO building or were you perhaps in the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were inside, in the small room inside the TO building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you see Grga Zubak in there?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So when he was put on the truck, he was taken out of the TO building and put onto the truck?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the small room.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Had he been crouching behind the door somewhere, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he was behind the door. He was in the left-hand corner, facing the door. That's where he and Mr. Izetbegovic were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And then Simo Zaric, Savo Cancarevic, and Mihaljo Topolovac entered that room; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing Simo Zaric on that occasion at all?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that night, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In any case, you were later on transferred to Brcko, and if I understand your testimony correctly, the conditions were better in Brcko as compared to those in Samac in the TO and the treatment you had there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now let me ask you another matter regarding this transfer. Do you remember, by any chance, who read out the names of the people who were to be transferred from the TO to Brcko?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Brcko, you said that on the following day, Simo Zaric came and took away Sulejman Tihic, and perhaps even Omer Nalic, back to Samac to give an interview, and then you went on to say what Tihic told you afterwards about it. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember saying that. I remember a hundred per cent that Simo Zaric came to Brcko then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, that's not contentious at all. Mr. Zaric did come to Brcko on the following day. However, he claims that on that occasion he didn't take with him either Sulejman Tihic or anybody else. He said that he simply came to ensure that you were doing well, that everybody arrived there well, and that he and other people brought with them apples, sandwiches, and cigarettes to be distributed to all of you who had been transferred from Samac, and that after several days, Sulejman Tihic was taken to Samac, but not in the company of Zaric. Some other persons took Tihic, Nalic, and Hadzialijagic with them on another occasion. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that I remembered with certainty that it was on the following day that Zaric came to Brcko but that I wasn't quite sure when were the others taken to give the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is something that fits with the information that we have. I would like to ask you a few questions regarding Esad Dagovic. You have already told us that Esad Dagovic was a very good friend of yours and that you knew him from your childhood.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We grew up together.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you said that you had talked to him and that Esad Dagovic was supposed to come to the States for a vacation and that this is what you talked about during your last conversation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you testified here and replied to questions put to you by Mr. Pantelic regarding (redacted) , and then you said that you followed all trials on Internet so far. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say that I followed all trials, but a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I presume that you, as somebody who is from Samac, would consider this case to be the most interesting one. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, "this case"?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean this current trial, the Samac trial, in which you're testifying.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And I suppose that you were mostly interested in this trial and that you followed this trial the most on Internet.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So did you follow this trial in real time?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with a 30-minute delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you must have heard what other witnesses said here.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard Dragan Delic, Kalaja Nusreta, so Nusret Kalaja, Safet Dagovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you by any chance follow the testimony of Kemal Mehinovic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness also -- the interpreters note, the witness also mentioned another name that we did not catch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The interpreters are saying there was another name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will slow down and I just have a couple of others -- well, let me check.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the name of Slavko Cuka [phoen] was mentioned but was not recorded. So can you please just confirm that for me. Is that in fact (redacted) ?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Prior to testifying here, you had information about what certain other witnesses said in evidence here before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if it was in public session, it was available to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned your grandmother's death in December 1993. At that point you were imprisoned in Batkovici. Were you allowed to attend your grandmother's funeral?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe I have to object to that. I mean, this is not related to my cross-examination, the death of his grandmother is one issue, the funeral is completely different issue. I don't believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lazarevic. It's the same. Mr. Weiner can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And a few other matters. Sir, you testified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We didn't get the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Sir, we didn't receive your answer as to whether or not you attended your grandmother's funeral, whether they let you attend the funeral.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. They did not allow me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, what I'd like to do is go over a few of the dates. There was a lot of discussion in relation to dates of certain situations that occurred. Now, there was some question as to when you first saw Miroslav Tadic, and you indicated in January of 1993. Previously, in your statement, you said the following, and I'd ask you if this refreshes your recollection or does this help clarify things to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wish to clarify, to try to be more precise about this. Since the witness saw Tadic on a number of occasions, I presume this question pertains to Batkovici, but could we please specify whether this refers to January of 1993 so that we don't confuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This refers to Batkovici, and in your statement, sir, on page 5, you state: "I stayed in Batkovici until 9 June 1994. During my stay in Batkovici, Tadic came several times. I think that the first time he came to Batkovici was December 1992 or January 1993." You made that statement in 1998. Based on that statement, is it possible that Miroslav Tadic -- that you had first seen Miroslav Tadic in December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I said that I thought I had seen him, but I'm not sure now. If you will allow me, I can explain to you why it is that I'm not certain about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Please explain.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in prison for a long time there, and we were beaten quite a lot and mistreated there. They separated me from my daughter for a whole two years. I couldn't think about the dates and try to retain the dates. All I thought about was whether I would live through the day, whether I will have enough food, whether we will be beaten on any given day. So all of these questions that have to do with the exact date, I don't know what normal person would be able to retain all that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue on. You indicated that you got to the primary school in May of 1992, and you thought you first saw Miroslav Tadic there in June of 1992. Since there was an exchange on May 26th, or towards the end of May, is it possible that you saw Miroslav Tadic in May of 1992 at the primary school?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that I did not remember the exact day when I saw Miroslav Tadic. It could have been between May or August/September, when we were transferred to the TO. I don't remember exactly what month it was, but you can find it in my statement. So during that time when I was in the elementary school, I saw him several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated or you talked about Miroslav Tadic receiving a bribe from Saban [phoen] Seric. Now, the record that was read to you concerns a December 24th, 1992 exchange involving an individual with the last name of Seric. The Saban Seric that you know, what -- approximately what was his date of birth, or what year was he born?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just give you an approximation. He was born in 1954 or 1956 or 1958, somewhere there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The list of December 24th, 1992, talks about a Sahan Seric, with a date of birth of 1950, who was the son of Hasan. Do you know that individual?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you with certainty. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Finally, counsel said to you that you didn't mention -- said to you in cross that you didn't mention the bribe to Miroslav Tadic from Sahan of Saban, sorry, Seric. Now, do you recall in your 1998 statement if you did, in fact, mention bribes being paid to Miroslav Tadic at Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I mentioned that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you recall saying the following: "If a person that was on Tadic's list was not present, maybe, because he was on forced labour, Tadic would cross out his name. Other detainees would then approach Tadic, give him money, and Tadic would walk out. Later, Tadic would come back and read the names of those who gave him money. I saw four or five detainees giving money to Tadic. He always accepted the money offered to him." Do you recall saying that in 1998 to the investigators or having that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And is that a true and accurate portrayal of what happened at Batkovici in relation to Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Subasic, for giving evidence to the Tribunal. We are now finished with you and you may go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We have three minutes to go. I think we've finished. Tomorrow we'll continue after the Status Conference in the afternoon, I think with Witness A. Yes. Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And Your Honour, just since we have a minute, there -- should Witness A finish with his cross-examination tomorrow, if we have enough time, then we will have another witness available to start straight away if that's what the Trial Chamber would like, because I appreciate that you said yesterday the witnesses could be released, but, in fact, we kept one of them here, and we can continue straight ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because the Prosecution earlier on had asked that they be released because nobody sure that we would finish. Yes. Very well. We will continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Just so you know that one is available should we have the time tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
